entries.main_competence: 1.  Demonstrate mastery of the principles of Computer Science
entries.specific_competence: 1.1  Demonstrate understanding of the principles of computer architecture and organisation
entries.learning_activity: (a)   Describe the classification of computer architecture (Von Neumann and Non Von Neumann, Harvard Architecture, Modified Harvard Architecture, Flynn’ s Taxonomy)
teaching_learning_activities: Brainstorming: Guide a student by using video tutorials, Internet or Library search to explore the classification of computer architecture.

TIPS: Lead students in manageable groups to describe the classifications of  each computer architecture(Overview, importance, and the role in modern computing systems.  Give concept of instruction set architecture (ISA) and its relationship to computer architecture.

Discuss features, advantages, and disadvantages, and how particular architectures are used in different devices (e.g., smartphones, supercomputers, embedded systems) and industries. Supplement information with diagrams, illustrations, real-life examples or applications that showcase the architecture’s strengths.)
Collaborative Project: Guide students by assigning them work to analyse, compare, and contrast different computer architectures.
entries.assessment: The classification of computer architecture is properly described
resources: Simulator creation tools (TopGen, Grey box, TopoMojo,vTunnel, etc)
entries.references: TIE, Computer Science for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 1.  Demonstrate mastery of the principles of Computer Science
entries.specific_competence: 1.1  Demonstrate understanding of the principles of computer architecture and organisation
entries.learning_activity: (b) Demonstrate understanding of  Boolean algebra and logic gates  (Logic expressions, standard logic gate symbols, logic circuits)
teaching_learning_activities: Demonstration/Scenario/Case study/Game: Guide students by using gamified learning platforms with educational games, scenarios or case studies to explore and demonstrate on Boolean algebra and Logic gates as physical devices in real life

Think-Ink-Pair- Share(TIPS): Lead students by using video tutorials, Internet or Library search to understand Boolean algebra and logic gates (importance in computer science, Boolean data types and operators,
theorems and laws, truth tables, logic gates, combinational logic circuits, etc.). Highlight how to implement logic gates and Boolean expressions in code
Experiment: Guide students to experiment with building and testing circuits using logic gate kits or simulation software

Collaborative Project: Guide students by assigning them creative projects that apply Boolean algebra and logic gates to solve real-world problems or challenges in their surrounding environment, such as design a simple security system or a traffic light controller using logic gates, etc
entries.assessment: Understanding of  Boolean algebra and logic gates  is correctly demonstrated
resources: Handouts with Boolean expressions and truth tables
entries.references: TIE, Computer Science for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 1.  Demonstrate mastery of the principles of Computer Science
entries.specific_competence: 1.1  Demonstrate understanding of the principles of computer architecture and organisation
entries.learning_activity: (c) Explore computer memory (Meaning, design principles,   memory hierarchy and interfacing, cache memory, memory mapping, primary & secondary memory)
teaching_learning_activities: Simulation/ virtual lab/Tutorial videos/ Case studies: Guide students in manageable groups by using Virtual lab, simulation, tutorial videos, or case study and real world examples to explore how computer memory is utilised in different scenarios (gaming, multitasks, data storage, etc).
TIPS: Lead students in manageable groups to explore computer memory and respective functions (build simple memory model using physical objects and simulate memory allocation using simulators)

Memory Simulation Game: Use or design a memory simulation game for students to play a role of computer processors accessing different memory units to retrieve data. Assign a tasks or challenges where students should make decisions based on memory hierarchy, such as fetching data from registers or retrieving data from secondary storage.
entries.assessment: Computer memory is properly explored
entries.references: TIE, Computer Science for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 1.  Demonstrate mastery of the principles of Computer Science
entries.specific_competence: 1.1  Demonstrate understanding of the principles of computer architecture and organisation
entries.learning_activity: (d) Analyse instruction set architecture (Instruction set types, registers, instruction execution cycles, addressing modes, register transfer language, ARM and x86 architectures)
teaching_learning_activities: Practical /Scenario/Simulation/ virtual lab: Lead students to explore the instruction set architecture in computer system using simulation, virtual lab, scenarios, case studies or alternatives

TIPS: Guide students in manageable groups to introduce concept of ISA; analyse instruction set architecture (design choices, performance trade-offs, and challenges associated with different ISAs) using Simulator, virtual lab or physical hardware. Relate ISAs to real-world examples on how they have influenced computing devices over time
Collaborative Project: Lead students by assigning them to design their own simple ISA and create an emulator for it
entries.assessment: Instruction set architecture is correctly analysed
entries.references: TIE, Computer Science for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 1.  Demonstrate mastery of the principles of Computer Science
entries.specific_competence: 1.1  Demonstrate understanding of the principles of computer architecture and organisation
entries.learning_activity: (g)  Develop understanding of pipelining (Basics, types, stalling & forwarding, throughput and speedup, hazards) and Instruction Level Parallelism ( concept, compilation techniques, scalar versus superscalar pipelining, branch prediction, register renaming) and thread and data level parallelism
teaching_learning_activities: TIPS and Simulation/ virtual lab/ video tutorials/ Internet or Library search

Guide students to explore the pipelining, Instruction Level Parallelism, and thread and data level parallelism using visual aids, diagrams, animations, simulations, and other alternatives for students to visualise the parallelism and pipeline stages and the movement of instructions

Discussion: Lead students in a manageable groups to discuss and understand the pipelining, Instruction Level Parallelism, and thread and data level parallelism by sharing real world examples and case studies where pipelining and parallelism used to improve performance.
Project work: Guide students by assigning projects that involve implementing simple pipelines, exploring ILP in code optimisation, or designing parallel algorithms.
entries.assessment: Understanding of the pipelining, Instruction Level Parallelism, and thread and data level parallelism is correctly developed
entries.references: TIE, Computer Science for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.learning_activity: (a) Demonstrate understanding of  OSI and TCP/IP Reference models, transmission media, wireless transmission, the public switched telephone networks, mobile telephone system and Network protocols (HTTP , FTP , IP ,PPP ,etc)

Discussion and Question and Answer: Ask individual students to elaborate the  OSI and TCP/IP Reference models (purpose, role of each layers in routing data packet, IP address in identify device, etc.)
entries.assessment: Understanding of Reference models and transmission media, wireless transmission, the public switched telephone networks, mobile telephone system and Network protocols is properly demonstrated
resources: Network devices (Router, Switch, Bridge, Repeater, Hub, Gateway, etc.)
entries.references: TIE, Computer Science for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 1.  Demonstrate mastery of the principles of Computer Science
entries.specific_competence: 1.2   Demonstrate understanding of computer networks
entries.learning_activity: (d) Develop understanding of Network layer (design issues, routing algorithms, Congestion control algorithms, Internetworking, the network layer in the internet (IPv4 and IPv6), Quality of Service)
teaching_learning_activities: Simulation/ virtual lab/ video tutorials/ Internet or Library search
Guide students to explore the network layer using specified or alternate technique/ method by relating with shared real world examples such as ICMP and ARP

Discussion: Lead students in a manageable groups  to understand the network layer (Purpose in OSI model, role in routing data packets between networks, importance, subnetting in dividing IP address to smaller networks, routing tables, recent advancement in network layer technologies).
Demonstration: Guide students to use a network simulation tool or an online platform to demonstrate routing concepts and configure routing tables
TIPS: Lead students to analyse case studies of network layer issues such as DDoS attacks or network congestion and their possible solutions

Collaborative Project: Guide students by assigning them project work such as to design a secure network architecture for a small business, analysing the performance of different routing protocols, etc
entries.assessment: Understanding of Network layer is correctly developed
entries.references: TIE, Computer Science for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 1.  Demonstrate mastery of the principles of Computer Science
entries.specific_competence: 1.2   Demonstrate understanding of computer networks
entries.learning_activity: (e) Elaborate the transport layer (Transport service, elements of transport protocol, Simple Transport Protocol, Internet transport layer protocols: UDP and TCP)
teaching_learning_activities: TIPS and Simulation/ virtual lab/ video tutorials/ Internet or Library search: Lead students in a manageable groups  to understand the transport layer by relating with shared real world examples such as UDP and TCP in online gaming, video streaming, video calling and web browsing

Discussion: Lead students in a manageable group to understand the transport layer (Purpose in OSI model, role in communication between devices, importance, ports, protocols-TCP and UDP, reliable against unreliable transmission).

Demonstration: Guide students to use a network simulation tool or an online platform to demonstrate the impact of packet loss and retransmission in TCP. Using reliable software to show network packet captures.

TIPS: Lead students to create their simple network protocol using basic principles of the transport layer using interactive software/ tools. Let them capture and analyse network traffic at the transport layer using network monitoring tool

Collaborative Project: Guide students by assigning them project works on a specific transport layer protocol such as TCP, UDP, and SCTP with focus to research on the features, advantages, and real-world applications.
entries.assessment: The transport layer is properly elaborated
entries.references: TIE, Computer Science for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 1.  Demonstrate mastery of the principles of Computer Science
entries.specific_competence: 1.2   Demonstrate understanding of computer networks
entries.learning_activity: (f)    Describe the application layer (Domain name system, electronic mail, World Wide Web: architecture; dynamic web document and http)
teaching_learning_activities: Simulation/ virtual lab/ video tutorials/ Internet or Library search: Lead students in a manageable groups  to understand the application layer by relating with shared real world examples such as social media platforms, video streaming, online gaming, etc through HTTP, FTP, or SMTP

Discussion: Lead students in a manageable groups  to understand the application layer (Purpose in OSI model, importance in computer networks, how instant messaging services, web browsers, email clients, etc depends on application layer).

TIPS: Lead students to explore simple applications that utilise the application layer (basic web page created using  HTML and CSS or simple chat application created using socket programming in a programming language like Python).
Collaborative Project: Guide students by assigning them project works on different application layer protocols such as HTTP, FTP, DNS, SNMP or SMTP, research each protocol and explain how it works.
entries.assessment: Application layer is clearly described
entries.references: TIE, Computer Science for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 1.  Demonstrate mastery of the principles of Computer Science
entries.specific_competence: 1.2   Demonstrate understanding of computer networks
entries.learning_activity: (g)    Apply network security principles, tools and protocols in computer networks
teaching_learning_activities: TIPS: Lead students to explore importance of network security, common network security threats and vulnerabilities, network security tools and protocols,  and best network security practices, etc

Practical / Simulation/ Virtual lab: Guide students into manageable groups to apply  network security principles, tools and protocols in computer networks (configure firewalls, perform security audits in simulated networks, and analyse network traffic using packet tracer or alternative network analysis tool)
Guest speakers and Field trip: Invite guest speaker from network security industry or organise field trips to help students to explore and experience real world security practices
Discussion: Guide students to analyse and discuss case studies on network security breaches and their consequences to society

Collaborative Project: Guide students by assigning them project works such as to create secure network configurations, developing security policies, or conducting vulnerability assessments using packet tracer or alternative network analysis tool.
entries.assessment: Network security principles, tools and protocols in computer network are applied correctly
entries.references: TIE, Computer Science for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

Discussion: Lead students in a manageable groups  to understand the concept of OS (types, roles and features, major milestones and advancements, etc).

TIPS: Lead students to explore and discuss real world scenarios that OS play critical roles (embedded systems, server management, or virtualisation, etc). Discuss how Internet of Things (IoT) and cloud computing devices rely on OSs for effective operation
entries.assessment: The concepts, structure and design of operating systems is properly described
entries.references: TIE, Computer Science for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 1.  Demonstrate mastery of the principles of Computer Science
entries.specific_competence: 1.6 Demonstrate understanding of principles of Operating Systems
entries.learning_activity: (b)   Describe the impact of operating system design on application system design and performance
teaching_learning_activities: Case studies/ Guest speaker: Guide students to understand various given case studies regarding the impact of operating system design on application system design and performance

Discussion: Guide students in manageable groups by providing to them OS or application case studies and analyse the impact of specific OS design on the performance and design of various application running on it

Collaborative Project: Guide students by assigning them project works on designing and implementing a simple application that will run on different operating systems. Lead them to research and report the challenges they face and behaviour and performance
entries.assessment: The impact of operating system design on application system design and performance is correctly described
entries.references: TIE, Computer Science for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 2.   Demonstrate mastery of the data management
entries.specific_competence: 2.1  Demonstrate mastery of Advanced principles of databases and database management systems
entries.learning_activity: (a)   Describe the basic concepts of Relational Database Design, ER Model, SQL, NoSQL, big data, and data warehouse.
teaching_learning_activities: Case studies/Guest speaker: Guide students through invited guest speaker, to understand various given case studies regarding the concept of Relational Database Design, ER Model, SQL, NoSQL, big data, and data warehouse relating with real world examples.
Discussion: Lead students in a manageable groups  to explore principles of relational database design such as E-R
modelling,  how to identify entities, attributes, and relationships, and create ER diagrams
Practical/simulation: Lead students to design database schemas and ER diagrams based on various scenarios in their surrounding environments
Demonstration: Guide students to introduce and demonstrate SQL and NoSQL databases with simple and complex queries, and appropriate NoSQL languages or APIs.

Collaborative Project: Guide students by assigning them project works that involve designing and implementing a database system, querying data using SQL, analysing big data, or developing a simple data warehouse
entries.assessment: Basic concepts of Relational Database Design, ER Model, SQL, NoSQL, big data, and data warehouse are correctly described
entries.references: TIE, Computer Science for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education
